- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast modestly to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent price spike is followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction by 5–10% of the spike magnitude.  
- In periods with high sentiment volatility, reduce forecast smoothness — favor mean reversion toward recent 7–14 day average.  
- If forecast consistently exceeds true outcome by 3–5% over 3–5 days, adjust downward by 1–2% per day to reflect diminishing momentum.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.6 → -0.3 → +0.4), reduce forecast volatility and favor mid-range values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after spike, reduce forecast slope in first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7) and forecast is erratic, apply smoothing filter to dampen noise.
